why: T-144 P0 LIVE FREEZE repair: the host dispatch point must be FAIL-OPEN independently of plugin correctness. The 2.3.0 seam `globalThis.__SPB?.(w,e=>H(e,w))` dropped every non-sync host event whenever the hook was absent (plugin import failure left __SPB uninstalled -> the original H dispatch never ran -> frozen TUI; the real user reproduced this). The 254-byte Lw window cannot hold the fail-open branch plus the exact original callback context (proven by exhaustive minimization, floor ~272 bytes), so clause 12 selects a LARGER exact structural window: 853 bytes covering Lw plus the byte-stable neighbours (Args provider, Permission provider, path import, Nw registry object, yj binary search, Xy comparator). Replacement semantics: hook PRESENT -> __SPB(w, e=>H(e,w)) (emit context is the SSE wrapper; the exact-host E-1266 run proved the visible store accepts it and the installed hook barrier forwards the original payload); hook ABSENT -> H(w.payload,{directory:w.directory,workspace:w.workspace}) exactly as the original host dispatch. Window bytes outside the corrected Lw are verbatim except two semantic-preserving shrink rewrites used solely to fund the fail-open branch (Permission init inlines its single cj() reference; yj uses (H+w)/2|0, identical to Math.floor for the non-negative indices this function handles).

anchor.offset_probe: exactly-once search; the recorded offset for both supported builds is 97762249 but the probe, not the number, is the authority

guards: anchor must occur exactly once in the source image
replacement must not be longer than the anchor
patched image must differ from the source only inside the anchor window
patched size must equal source size
patched image must NOT contain the original uncorrected Lw dispatch
patched image must contain exactly one fail-open dispatch site (hook-present + hook-absent branches)
restore_contract: Restore puts back the recorded original bytes of bin/opencode.exe (state.json original_hashes backup).
